_about: Canonical shared rule set for prose-lint. The rule CONTENT lives here (data); the lint HARNESS reads it (backend/app/services/prose_lint.py in this app; scripts/prose-lint.py in federal-proposal-assistant and federal-proposal-copilot, which pull this file via their sync scripts). A rule added here propagates to every consumer with no per-app code edit. Keep the term lists in spirit-sync with knowledge/doctrine/prohibited-claims-doctrine.md and PROSE-QUALITY-DOCTRINE.md.
_severity_policy: term_lists.process_terms and patterns.em_dash and the section-sign glyph are HIGH. Everything else is ADVISORY. (How each consumer maps HIGH/ADVISORY to blocking is the consumer's policy: the FPA/copilot CLI gate exits 1 on HIGH; this app emits high/medium ReviewFindings.)

meta_commentary: a capability we do not hold

_pattern_notes.negation_dismissal: Catches '...so no X is required' — a sentence whose payload is a non-event. Known false positive: a negative conclusion that has no affirmative form ('IRB review therefore does not apply'). ADVISORY, so it informs rather than blocks. Added 2026-08-18 from the arl-collaborative-aitr-sbir volume, where five instances survived two editorial passes because no mechanical rule existed.
_pattern_notes.raise_then_permit: Catches 'X is not required ... Y is acceptable'. Requires BOTH halves so a bare scope limit ('no VLA is proposed in Phase I') is not flagged.
_pattern_notes.capability_denial: ADVISORY. Self-limiting capability statements: telling the customer what we do not have or have not measured. Adopted 2026-08-31 (EdgeRunner). A proposal states how it meets a requirement, or how it will meet it; it does not enumerate the requirements it misses. Convert, do not delete: 'masking is not a current capability' becomes 'on-device masking is designed, built, and tested under the prototype'. Deliberately does NOT match negatives that carry a POSITIVE claim ('No model participates in the verification check', 'no telemetry egress', 'closed-book generation is disabled') — those say the offeror is better, not worse. Also deliberately does not match the status value 'partially met', which is legitimate in a compliance matrix.
_pattern_notes.claim_withdrawal: ADVISORY. Same family as capability_denial: prose that pulls a claim back after making it ('not claimed at TRL 7', 'a demonstration rather than a contract delivery', 'does not guarantee', 'neither transfers'). State the maturation path or the delivery path instead. Accreditation scope is the one place a boundary limit is load-bearing — restate it as what the prototype delivers rather than as a denial, and keep prohibited-claim rules (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001) intact.
_pattern_notes.contrast_construction: ADVISORY, density-based. Counts 'not X but Y', ', not Y.', 'rather than', 'instead of' per 1,000 words and fires above thresholds.contrast_per_1000_words. Adopted 2026-09-02 (NAVWAR EPSS): the brief carried 18 in 3,600 words and a blind reviewer said it read like a debate brief. Each instance is fine alone; the density is the finding. Keep the load-bearing ones.
_pattern_notes.bullet_ratio: ADVISORY, computed by the harness from paragraph shape, no regex. Share of body WORDS that sit in list items. Fires below thresholds.bullet_ratio_low (a wall of prose that cannot be skimmed) and above thresholds.bullet_ratio_high (a paper rewritten as bullets). Adopted 2026-09-02: the same brief went from 0% to 53% and back with nothing measuring it. The Mystic Depot Phase I briefs that advanced sat at 42% of PARAGRAPHS, roughly 20-25% of words.
_pattern_notes.ai_tell_terms: ADVISORY term list. Seeded from phrases reviewers explicitly called 'an AI tell' on NAVWAR EPSS (Jack FitzGerald, 2026-09-01) plus the usual suspects. Add to it whenever a reviewer names one; do not pad it with words that merely sound corporate.
